newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrafina consulted Suez/Lyonnaise on share buy.
newsitem.headline: Electrafina consulted Suez/Lyonnaise on share buy.

text.p: Belgian financier Albert Frere, head of Belgian holding company Electrafina consulted Gerard Mestrallet, the future head of the soon-to-be formed Suez / Lyonnaise des Eaux group, before boosting his Electrafina stake in the new group, Mestrallet told Reuters on Wednesday.

"Mr Frere always calls me before buying shares in our group. We always act in concert," he said after the annual meeting of shareholders in utility holding company Tractebel SA of which he is chairman.
Frere said on Tuesday that Electrafina's equity stake in the new group was now nine percent.
Sources close to Electrafina said the company recently bought three percent in Lyonnaise on the Paris bourse.
Electrafina had never before said how much it owned in the new group. Electrafina had said it had 11.35 percent in Suez alone.
"This makes Albert Frere one of the leading shareholders (in Suez/Lyonnaise)," he said.
Electrafina is a unit of Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL), controlled by Frere.
Mestrallet said that French group Credit Agricole would have a direct 7.6 percent stake in the merged group and another 1.5 and two percent via funds under its control.
